judgments.catchwords: Keywords: Dispute involved contentious inheritance dispute between the Plaintiffs and the Defendants on the estate – The Deceased’s death was recorded as 14.10.2018 while abroad in Taiwan, died as a Muslim without a Will – The Deceased left behind immovable properties, various cash savings and deposits and holding in businesses and unincorporated enterprises – The 1st and 4th Plaintiffs are siblings and the beneficiaries to the Deceased’s estate – The 5th Plaintiff is the Deceased’s younger sister and also the administrator of the estate of Noraini binti Janum – Noraini binti Janum is the mother of the Deceased – The 1st Defendant, Diman bin Hassan is the husband of the Deceased and the father of the 1st – 4th Plaintiffs. The 1st Defendant is the current administrator of the Deceased’s estate – The 2nd Defendant, Siti Fatimah binti Diman, is the Deceased’s biological daughter and the eldest sister of the 1st – 4th Plaintiffs – The Plaintiffs, who are the Deceased’s children and siblings, alleged that the 1st Defendant, who is the husband of the Deceased, committed among others fraud and mismanagement to secure sole control of the assets of the Deceased – The 1st Defendant on the other hand averred that the assets were distributed equally among the children with their consent – The 1st Defendant stated that the filing of this suit by the Plaintiffs was based on the 1st Defendant’s intention to remarry – Agreed Issues – Fraud – Fraud for dissipation of assets – Forger – the crux of the Plaintiffs’ case rests on allegations of fraud, fabrication of documents, and forgery – The Defendant’s defence is that the renunciation documents of the Plaintiffs as administrators were done accordingly and are valid - Absence of Expert Evidence - Failure to Lodge a Police Report – Identification of Forger – it was the 1st – 4th Plaintiffs contention that they were induced to sign blank papers which were then used as documents – the Court finds it improbable that individuals of such academic standing could be induced into signing “blank signature pages” without understanding the legal significance of their actions – the Defendants provided evidence that the Plaintiffs initially conceded and agreed to the 1st Defendant’s (D1) appointment as sole administrator – their subsequent challenge, years after the grant was extracted, appears to be driven by a change of heart following D1’s decision to remarry, rather than a genuine lack of initial consent – Validity of the Distribution Arrangement (Takharruj) – the 1st Defendant contended that the distribution of the estate followed a family agreement consistent with the Islamic principle of takharruj – D1 testified that the distribution – which provided the children with equal shares of immovable properties while he retained the movable assets for business operations – was a mutually discussed arrangement intended for the long-term benefit of the family – the Court accepts D1’s explanation that the movable assets were used as working capital to maintain the family businesses – the Court finds that D1 followed established judgments.catchwords: Criminal Justice - Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, ss. 2, 37(d), 39B(1)(a) — Trafficking — Appeal against conviction — Whether statutory presumption of deemed possession under s. 37(d) can be conflated with substantive trafficking under s. 2 by "keeping and storing" without proof of an independent positive overt act beyond reasonable doubt — Presumption stacking and impermissible inversion of burden of proof — Criminal Procedure Code, s. 180(3) — Duty of trial court to amend charge to possession under s. 39A(2) where only s. 37(d) possession proved at close of prosecution case — Mid-trial mutation of case causing incurable prejudice and breach of natural justice — Evidence Act 1950, s. 54(1) — Prejudicial reception of bad character evidence (AADK document and smoking bong) — Break in chain of custody via non-contemporaneous, post-facto reconstruction of Drug Exhibit Register (POL 260) compromising identity of dangerous drugs — Non-exclusive access to ancestral premises and negative forensic nexus — Curative provisions inapplicable where foundational evidence of possession is fatally tainted — Conviction quashed and substituted conviction under s. 39A(2) refused — Accused acquitted and discharged.

judgments.title: Peoplender Sdn. Bhd. v Tan Jian Ho
judgments.catchwords: Civil Procedure & Appealability of Interlocutory Orders – Summary judgment dismissal – Section 28(1)(b) Courts of Judicature Act 1964 – Interlocutory order – Substantive right exception – Irreversible prejudice – MT Ventures principle – Whether an appeal against a Magistrate's Court's dismissal of a summary judgment application is competent despite the general statutory restriction on interlocutory appeals under Section 28(1)(b) of the CJA 1964 – Whether refusing summary judgment effectively deprives a plaintiff of a contractually bargained-for "conclusive evidence" mechanism, thereby creating a final and irreversible prejudice that falls within the MT Ventures exception. Summary Judgment (Order 14) & Evidentiary Burdens – Order 14 Rules of Court 2012 – Prima facie case – Bona fide triable issue – Shadowy defence – Bare denial – Certificate of Indebtedness – Conclusive evidence clause – Shifting burden of proof – Cempaka Finance principle – Whether a defendant's bare denial of an electronic signature, unsupported by a police report, digital forensics, or specific particulars of fraud, is sufficient to establish a bona fide triable issue under Order 14 – Whether a contractually agreed Certificate of Indebtedness successfully shifts the burden of proof to the defendant to demonstrate fraud, manifest error, or bad faith in an adjectival law context. Guarantee, Indemnity & Corporate Liability – Letter of Guarantee and Indemnity – Personal liability – Continuing guarantee – Principal debtor obligation – Cessation of directorship – Independent contractual obligation – Whether a guarantor's personal, independent liability under a Letter of Guarantee and Indemnity is extinguished or diminished by their subsequent resignation or cessation as a director of the primary corporate debtor. Banking, Finance & Regulatory Frameworks – Peer-to-Peer (P2P) financing platform – Securities Commission of Malaysia (SC) – Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 – Guidelines on Recognized Markets – Moneylenders Act 1951 – Illegal moneylending – Whether a financing transaction operated by an SC-licensed Peer-to-Peer (P2P) platform falls under the regulatory ambit of the Moneylenders Act 1951, or if it operates under a distinct, separate statutory framework. Administration of Justice & Case Management Principles – Order 1A Rules of Court 2012 – Overriding objective – Expeditious and efficient resolution – Instrument of delay – Contrived defences – Whether sending a matter to full trial on highly delayed and legally meritless assertions violates the mandatory court obligation to handle cases justly, expeditiously, and efficiently under Order 1A.
